answer: Best sybil defense: randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. An agent's work is scored each epoch by a panel drawn by verifiable random function from the validator pool, so attackers never know which judges review a submission. Collusion only pays if the faker bribes the exact panel members, and since panels reshuffle each epoch (cohorts: onyx, saffron, tide), influence must be bought repeatedly against new strangers, while captured panels are re-audited next cohort. Attack cost scales with pool size, so faking identity stays unprofitable.
